purpose: Post hoc size-matched sensitivity analysis of archived paired RECTANGLE SAC statistics, without new cipher evaluations
selection_disclosure: Conditions and motivation were informed by the already inspected 2026-11-10 cipher results. This is not an independent replication or a blinded preregistration. This plan and execution source will be committed before the new calibration/validation simulations.
rng: NumPy PCG64 SeedSequence; [base_seed,401,n,N,bank] calibration; [base_seed,402,n,N] validation; [base_seed,403,n,N,method_index] cipher randomizers; [base_seed,404,n,N,method_index] validation randomizers; [base_seed,405,bank,policy_index,N,round,method_index] paired bootstrap
primary_rule: Count retains its exact discrete decision p_exact+delta_A < 0.001. Let s_N be its exact iid-label rejection probability. Histogram tests use the unchanged plus-one rank rule including ties, (1+G+E)/(B+1) < s_N, so both have a reference ceiling s_N+delta_A. Their conditional realized sizes are independently validated, not assumed equal.
secondary_rule: Set a=0.001-delta_A. Count uses exact randomized p=P(V>v)+U*P(V=v). Histogram uses randomized rank p=(G+U*(E+1))/(B+1), G=#calibration strictly greater and E=#calibration equal. Reject p<a. Under label-model exchangeability these p-values are marginally uniform, including discrete ties. Conditional sizes can still vary with the trained bank.
randomization: Independent uniforms across methods and replicate indices; shared across rounds and calibration banks to isolate calibration variation. Randomization is an explicitly modified secondary detector, not the archived count rule.
null_model: Unchanged independent-label SAC null, iid Bin(N,1/2) matrix cells. Simulate row multinomial histograms as sufficient statistics for Basic and maximum-axis laws. Row and Column share only a marginal maximum-axis null law. Simulated count values are separate marginal binomial draws; no paired cross-detector null conclusions are made.
finite_domain_bound: Unchanged delta_A=[N(n+1)]^2/2^n, bounding input-star overlap and random-function/permutation switching. Ideal-label size matching is approximate for the ideal-permutation reference within this bound.
archive_design: Retain the largest 5000 Basic/max-axis values per training bank, with B recorded; this suffices for all predeclared decisions below alpha=0.001. Retain validation upper tails with original indices, a full count-frequency histogram and all count boundary candidates. Record SHA256 of full generated arrays, seeds and source, and check tail-versus-full rejection equality at execution. These are marginal-null sufficient records, not saved full cipher experiments.
validation: One new held-out sample per (n,N), shared across banks. Report Wilson 95% conditional intervals, target ratios and residual mismatch. No validation-guided threshold tuning, seed selection or stopping. Banks 1/2 are retraining sensitivity, never replacements for bank 0.
inference: Analyze all 15 archived RECTANGLE round/sample conditions, giving 45 count-versus-histogram contrasts per policy/bank. Primary inference is bank 0 match_count_nonrandom, with exact paired McNemar tests and Holm n=90 (45 tested RECTANGLE plus 45 untested CLEFIA assigned p=1), retaining the original grid's multiplicity factor. Other policies/banks are sensitivity analyses, not extra independent confirmations.
intervals: Pointwise Wilson intervals for rates and 10000 paired multinomial bootstrap draws for rate differences. Conditional on a trained bank; bootstrap does not include calibration retraining or key variation. Zero discordances can yield degenerate bootstrap intervals and do not prove equivalence.
reporting: Archive full grids, discordances, paired differences, conditional intervals, p-values, held-out null rates, target sizes and bank ranges; show both focus conditions and any reversal/non-significant result. Compare with unchanged original calibration as a historical benchmark. No universal detector ranking or all-key generalization.
limitations: Existing cipher inputs and one default key are reused. This experiment addresses null-size confounding and calibration sensitivity, not key robustness or a cryptographic explanation. Three training banks describe observed variation, not a precise distribution of retraining uncertainty. Actual false-positive rates in deterministic ciphers are not estimated by ideal-null simulation. No manuscript Word edit is part of this execution.
